title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck defines a 'catégorie polynômiale'. It is a category P with finite products, together with a wide, non-full subcategory P_1 of 'admissible' (linear) arrows. P_1 has the same objects as P, is closed under composition, contains the identities, and is additive. Products in P are products in P_1, and an arrow into X×Y is admissible iff its components are. As a consequence each hom-set P(X,Y) is an abelian group. It is additive in the precomposed variable, (f+g)∘h = f∘h + g∘h, but not in the other, since f∘(g+h) ≠ f∘g + f∘h in general. The multiplicative monoid Z^× acts on every object by n·id_X.

This page states axiom d), a weight grading.
- For r = 1: P(X,Y) = ⊕_{n≥0} P_n(X,Y), with f_n∘(λ id_X) = λ^n f_n for all λ ∈ Z. P_n is the group of 'homogeneous polynomial maps of degree n'.
- Multivariable form (*): P(X_1×…×X_r, Y) = ⊕_{n∈N^r} P_n(X_1,…,X_r;Y), with f∘(λ_1 id_{X_1},…,λ_r id_{X_r}) = λ_1^{n_1}…λ_r^{n_r} f. This is a multidegree decomposition.

Remark on uniqueness. Grothendieck starts a lemma, later struck through with diagonal lines. Take an abelian group P with a monoid homomorphism u: (Z^×)^r → End(P). If P = ⊕ P_n is a decomposition into 'weight spaces' for the characters λ ↦ λ^n, then the decomposition is unique and P_n is the simultaneous eigenspace {f : u(λ)f = λ^n f for all λ}. The proof sketch, continued on the next page: if g ∈ P_{n'} also has weight n, then (λ^n − λ^{n'})g = 0 for all λ. It would then suffice that the integers λ^n − λ^{n'} generate the unit ideal.

This fails. By Fermat, λ^p ≡ λ mod p for every integer λ; for example 6 divides λ^3 − λ. So on torsion groups the weights are not separated by integer scalars. A concrete counterexample: Z/2 can be declared to be of degree 1 or of degree 2. This is the 'canular arithmétique' (arithmetic joke) that Grothendieck flags.

His fix, on the next page:
- Demand the structure after every base change h (any commutative ring or Z-algebra), with P_h(X,Y) = P(X,Y) ⊗ h and λ ∈ (h^×)^r. In effect this is a G_m^r-comodule (Z[t^{±1}]-graded) structure, in the spirit of Roby's polynomial laws, where functoriality in all algebras is exactly what rescues polynomial maps from finite-field degeneracies.
- Alternatively, take the decomposition (*) as extra data.

He then adds the remaining axioms:
- e) degrees multiply under substitution;
- f) symmetry under permutation of factors;
- g) 'constant maps do not depend on the source', P_0(0,Y) ≅ P_0(X,Y);
- the notion of an h-polynomial category.

Purpose: an axiomatic framework for non-additive (polynomial) operations. In the cote's context these would be multiplicative structures (cup products, power operations) on semi-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes and their dévissage.
errors: The proof strategy of the struck lemma is wrong as stated: the elements λ^n − λ^{n'} (λ ∈ Z^r) need not generate the unit ideal of Z. By Fermat's little theorem p divides λ^p − λ, and 6 divides λ^3 − λ. Uniqueness of the weight decomposition fails for groups with torsion (e.g. Z/2 in degree 1 vs degree 2). Grothendieck evidently noticed this (the 'canular arithmétique'), struck the lemma, and replaced it by a base-change condition or by taking the grading as data.
Minor inconsistency with the previous page, where the Z-action is written μ_n(f) = f∘(n id_Y). For f: X→Y, precomposition requires n·id_X, as correctly written here in d).

ideas.what: Category with finite products whose hom-sets are abelian groups additive only under precomposition, with a distinguished wide subcategory of additive ('linear') maps compatible with products
ideas.modern_name: Cartesian left-additive category, with its subcategory of additive/linear maps

ideas.what: Grading of hom-sets into homogeneous components of (multi)degree n, characterized by f∘(λ·id) = λ^n f
ideas.modern_name: Weight/degree decomposition under the scalar (G_m) action; homogeneous polynomial maps; cf. Eilenberg–MacLane degree of functors, strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–MacLane (1954) for degree of functors; Roby (1963) for homogeneous polynomial laws; Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Observation that integer scalars do not separate weights in the presence of torsion (Fermat), so one must require the structure functorially for all base rings h, with λ ∈ h^×
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial laws (lois polynômes) vs polynomial maps; G_m-comodule structure vs Z^×-action

ideas.what: Uniqueness lemma for decompositions into eigenspaces for the characters λ ↦ λ^n of the multiplicative monoid
ideas.modern_name: Weight-space decomposition, cf. Adams-operation eigenspaces in λ-rings

missed.claim: Around 1975–76 Grothendieck axiomatizes 'polynomial categories': a finite-product category with abelian hom-groups that are left-additive only, plus a wide subcategory of additive maps compatible with products. This is essentially the notion of a Cartesian left-additive category with its linear maps (Blute–Cockett–Seely 2009), here enriched with a multi-degree grading. He links it to multiplicative structures on semi-simplicial complexes, i.e. to Dold–Puppe-type non-additive functors.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Graded left-additive categories are a natural setting for abelian functor calculus and Cartesian differential categories (Bauer–Johnson–Osborne–Riehl–Tebbe). Grothendieck's homogeneous-degree axioms (e)–(g) give a variant aimed at power operations and dévissage that the later literature seems not to have formulated in this form.

missed.claim: The uniqueness question for the grading over Z is left unresolved. Grothendieck replaces it either by a base-change condition over all Z-algebras or by taking the grading as extra structure. The theory of 'catégories polynômiales' (and h-polynomial categories) is not developed further in published form.
missed.quote: Cette décomposition n'est [pas] unique, en vertu de canulars "arithmétiques"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the same issue that separates polynomial functors from strict polynomial functors (Friedlander–Suslin), i.e. the torsion phenomena of functor cohomology. An axiomatic categorical treatment along these lines could unify them.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine weight-decomposition axiom plus a self-corrected uniqueness lemma. Its interest lies in the surrounding definition, an early (c. 1975) anticipation of Cartesian left-additive categories with a polynomial grading, apparently absent from Grothendieck's published work.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'Cette décomposition' most likely reads 'n'est pas unique' ('n'' and 'pas unique' written above the line), not '{+unique+}'. This is consistent with 'en vertu de canulars "arithmétiques"' and with the struck lemma.
'il se servait' is more plausibly 'il serait' / 'elle le serait', continuing on the next page with '…en exigeant qu'on ait, pour toute Z-algèbre h…'.

The whole block from 'Lemme' to the bottom of the page is struck through with diagonal lines, and 'Pour n=(n_1,…,n_r)∈Z' is separately crossed out; the transcription marks the lemma as deleted, which is correct.
In the lemma, u: (Z^×)^r → End(P) is a homomorphism of (multiplicative) monoids. The last line reads 'Or on a aussi u(λ)g_{n'} = λ_1^{n'_1}…λ_r^{n'_r} g_{n'}'.
